name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
description:
Detects abuse of elevation control mechanisms for privilege escalation:
- UAC bypass techniques on Windows
- Sudo abuse or sudoers file modification on Linux
- SetUID/SetGID binary manipulation
- Exploitation of elevated COM objects
- Token manipulation to gain elevated privileges
- Bypass of macOS authorization mechanisms
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate elevation requests are common in administrative workflows.

Common false positives:
- Administrators using UAC prompts for legitimate tasks
- Software installers requiring elevated permissions
- Developers using sudo for build or deployment tasks

Reduce false positives by:
- Monitoring for known UAC bypass binaries (fodhelper, eventvwr, sdclt)
- Flagging sudoers file modifications outside of change management
- Detecting SetUID changes on non-standard binaries
- Correlating with suspicious parent process chains

name: Account Manipulation Detection
description: Detects unauthorized account manipulation including permission escalation, group membership changes, credential policy modifications, and unauthorized role assignments in smart city management systems
false_positive_notes:
Routine HR onboarding, role changes, and IT administration tasks involve
legitimate account modifications. Correlate with HR workflows, ticketing
systems, and change management records to filter authorized changes.

name: Active Scanning Detection
description:
Detects active scanning and probing activity against smart city infrastructure:
- Port scanning across multiple hosts or services
- Vulnerability scanning signatures (Nmap, Nessus, Masscan)
- Service version enumeration
- Rapid connection attempts to non-existent services
- ICMP sweep and ARP scanning activity
false_positive_notes:
Network monitoring and asset discovery tools may trigger this rule.

Common false positives:
- Authorized vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys)
- Network monitoring tools performing health checks
- Load balancers probing backend services

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known scanner IPs and scheduled scan windows
- Excluding authorized vulnerability assessment tools
- Establishing baselines for normal network discovery patterns

name: Archive Collected Data Detection
description:
Detects archiving and compression of collected data indicating preparation
for exfiltration from smart city systems:
- Creation of compressed archives in staging directories
- Password-protected or encrypted archive creation
- Archiving of sensitive configuration, credential, or telemetry data
- Use of built-in compression utilities (tar, zip, gzip, rar, 7z)
- Split archive creation for easier exfiltration
false_positive_notes:
Data archiving is common for backups and file transfers.

Common false positives:
- Backup software creating scheduled archives
- Developers packaging project files for deployment
- Log rotation compressing old log files

Reduce false positives by:
- Monitoring for archives created in temp or staging directories
- Flagging password-protected archives (uncommon for legitimate backups)
- Detecting archive creation followed by network upload
- Correlating with prior data collection or discovery activity
- Alerting on archives containing system configuration or credential files

name: Automated Data Collection Detection
description: Detects automated data collection and scraping activities including bulk database queries, mass file access, and systematic data harvesting from smart city information systems
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate data analytics pipelines, backup processes, and reporting tools
may trigger this rule. Whitelist authorized ETL processes, backup agents,
and business intelligence tools by their service accounts and source IPs.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
description:
Detects persistence mechanisms via boot or logon autostart locations:
- Registry Run/RunOnce key modifications
- Startup folder additions
- Login items or launch agents on macOS/Linux
- Winlogon helper DLL modifications
- Boot configuration changes (BCD, GRUB)
- Authentication package registration
false_positive_notes:
Software installations commonly add autostart entries.

Common false positives:
- Legitimate software adding itself to startup (browsers, chat clients)
- Group Policy applying startup scripts
- System updates modifying boot configuration

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known software vendors and signed binaries
- Monitoring for unsigned or obfuscated binaries in autostart locations
- Flagging autostart entries pointing to temp or user directories
- Correlating with recent malware download or exploitation events

name: Brute Force Authentication Detection
description: Detects multiple failed authentication attempts from a single source IP, indicating credential brute force attack

name: Command and Control Beaconing Detection
description: Detects periodic outbound connections to external IPs indicating C2 beaconing activity

name: Windows Event Logs Cleared
description:
Detects clearing of Windows event logs, a common post-compromise activity
to remove evidence of malicious actions. Monitors wevtutil, PowerShell
Clear-EventLog, and WMI-based log clearing methods.
technique_name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
false_positive_notes:
Event log clearing has limited legitimate use cases.

Possible false positives:
- Scheduled maintenance scripts clearing old logs
- System troubleshooting by IT administrators
- Disk space management on log servers
- Application-specific log rotation

Reduce false positives by:
- Requiring justification for Security log clearing
- Whitelisting approved log management tools
- Monitoring for clearing outside maintenance windows
- Flagging clearing of Security log (almost always suspicious)
- Detecting rapid clearing of multiple logs
- Correlating with recent authentication or privilege escalation events
- Alerting on clearing immediately after suspicious activity

NOTE: Clearing of Security event log should almost always generate an alert
unless performed by authorized log management systems.

name: Clipboard Data Collection Detection
description: Detects clipboard monitoring and data collection activities indicating credential theft, sensitive data harvesting, or information gathering from smart city operator workstations
false_positive_notes:
Clipboard managers, password managers, and remote desktop clipboard
redirection are legitimate uses of clipboard APIs. Maintain an approved
application list and monitor for unexpected processes accessing clipboard data.

name: Cloud API Abuse Detection
description: Detects cloud API abuse including unauthorized API key usage, excessive API calls from unknown sources, cloud resource manipulation, and suspicious cloud management actions targeting smart city cloud infrastructure
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate cloud automation, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure-as-code
deployments may generate high API call volumes. Whitelist authorized service
accounts, CI/CD runner IPs, and correlate with deployment schedules.

name: Suspicious CMD Execution for Reconnaissance
description:
Detects suspicious cmd.exe execution patterns commonly used for system
reconnaissance, credential access preparation, and data staging.
Monitors for net.exe, reg.exe, systeminfo, whoami, and other discovery commands.
technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
false_positive_notes:
System administrators and automated scripts may legitimately use these commands.

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known admin accounts and service accounts
- Excluding scheduled tasks that run system inventory scripts
- Monitoring for rapid succession (5+ commands in 5 minutes)
- Correlating with unusual login times or source IPs

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter Abuse
description:
Detects suspicious use of command and scripting interpreters on smart city systems:
- PowerShell with encoded commands or download cradles
- Python, Bash, or JavaScript executing from unusual paths
- Script interpreters spawned by unexpected parent processes
- Obfuscated script content or base64-encoded payloads
- Interpreter execution with network activity or credential access
false_positive_notes:
Scripting interpreters are widely used for legitimate automation.

Common false positives:
- DevOps automation scripts using PowerShell or Python
- Scheduled tasks executing batch or shell scripts
- Developers running scripts during development

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known automation service accounts
- Focusing on encoded commands and download cradles
- Monitoring for interpreters spawned by unusual parents (e.g., Word, Excel)
- Correlating with network connections to external IPs

name: Suspicious Account Creation
description:
Detects creation of user accounts across smart city systems for persistence:
- Local, domain, and cloud account creation
- Accounts created with elevated privileges
- Accounts created outside of normal provisioning workflows
- Hidden or service accounts created by unauthorized processes
- Rapid account creation followed by immediate login
false_positive_notes:
Account creation is routine for onboarding and service deployment.

Common false positives:
- IT provisioning systems creating employee accounts
- Automated service account creation during deployments
- Lab environments spinning up test accounts

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known provisioning systems and their source IPs
- Flagging accounts created with administrative privileges
- Monitoring for account creation outside business hours
- Detecting accounts created by interactive sessions on servers

name: Suspicious Local Account Creation
description:
Detects creation of local user accounts with suspicious characteristics:
- Accounts added to privileged groups (Administrators, Remote Desktop Users)
- Hidden accounts (username ending with $)
- Accounts with passwords set to never expire
- Rapid account creation followed by privilege escalation
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate account creation occurs during:
- IT onboarding processes
- Automated provisioning systems
- Service account creation

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known IT administrator workstations
- Excluding accounts created by trusted provisioning tools
- Monitoring for accounts immediately added to Administrators group
- Flagging accounts created outside business hours
- Detecting unusual naming patterns (short names, numeric suffixes)
- Correlating with unauthorized login sources
- Alert on hidden accounts (ending with $) unless from domain controller

name: Credential Dumping Detection
description: Detects credential dumping attempts by identifying suspicious access to credential stores, authentication databases, and memory dumps
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate credential management tools (password managers, identity providers,
authentication services) may generate false positives. Whitelist known credential
management systems and monitor for deviations from normal access patterns.

name: Suspicious Data Archiving Activity
description:
Detects archiving of data that may indicate preparation for exfiltration:
- Large archive creation in unusual locations
- Password-protected or encrypted archives
- Archives containing sensitive directories (Documents, Desktop, AppData)
- Split archives (volume spanning)
- Archiving during off-hours or by unauthorized users
technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
false_positive_notes:
Data archiving is common for legitimate purposes.

Common false positives:
- Users creating personal backups
- File transfers for legitimate business purposes
- Software installations using compressed archives
- Automated backup solutions
- Developers archiving project files

Reduce false positives by:
- Threshold for archive size (> 50 MB more suspicious)
- Whitelisting known backup software
- Monitoring for archives in temporary directories
- Flagging password-protected archives (less common for personal use)
- Detecting archives followed by network upload
- Correlating with data exfiltration indicators
- Excluding archives to network shares or known backup locations
- Monitoring for archiving of system directories (Program Files, Windows)

Risk scoring:
- Small archive to user directory: Low
- Large archive to Temp: Medium
- Password-protected archive to Temp: High
- Encrypted archive + network upload: Critical

name: Data Destruction Detection
description: Detects data destruction activities including mass file deletion, disk wiping, database truncation, and deliberate data corruption targeting smart city operational data and configuration stores
false_positive_notes:
Scheduled data retention cleanup, log rotation, and database maintenance
operations may trigger this rule. Coordinate with database administrators
and implement change management approval for bulk deletion operations.

name: Data Exfiltration Detection
description: Detects large outbound data transfers indicating data exfiltration activity

name: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) Detection
description: Detects DDoS attacks by identifying high-volume traffic from multiple source IPs targeting a single destination IP or service within a short time window
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate traffic spikes during peak hours or special events may trigger this rule.
Consider adjusting thresholds for high-traffic services or implementing rate limiting
to reduce false positives from legitimate distributed access patterns.

name: Defacement Detection
description: Detects web defacement and content manipulation attacks targeting smart city public-facing portals, dashboards, and citizen information systems
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate content updates, CMS deployments, and authorized website
maintenance may trigger this rule. Implement file integrity monitoring
on web roots and coordinate with web development teams for change windows.

name: Security Tools Disabled or Modified
description:
Detects attempts to disable or modify security tools and defensive mechanisms:
- Windows Defender real-time protection disabled
- Security services stopped or disabled
- Firewall disabled via netsh or PowerShell
- Event logging disabled
- UAC settings weakened
- Security product exclusions added
technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate administrative activities may trigger this rule.

Common false positives:
- IT administrators troubleshooting security software
- Software installations temporarily disabling AV
- Maintenance scripts managing services
- Group Policy changes affecting security settings

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known maintenance windows
- Excluding IT admin workstations during approved changes
- Monitoring for MULTIPLE security impairments (threshold ≥ 2)
- Flagging defense evasion outside business hours
- Detecting rapid succession of security disablement
- Correlating with other attack indicators (process injection, lateral movement)
- Requiring re-enablement verification for legitimate changes

name: DLL Side-Loading Detection
description: Detects DLL side-loading attacks where adversaries place malicious DLLs alongside legitimate applications to achieve code execution within smart city control systems
false_positive_notes:
Software updates and legitimate application installations may load DLLs
from non-standard paths. Maintain an approved software baseline and hash
whitelist for known legitimate DLL files in the environment.

name: DNS Tunneling Detection
description: Detects DNS tunneling activity by identifying anomalous DNS query patterns, high-entropy domain names, and excessive DNS traffic from a single host indicative of covert C2 communication channels
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate DNS-based services (e.g., DNS-over-HTTPS clients, dynamic DNS updates)
may trigger this rule. Review query frequency and payload sizes to differentiate
between legitimate traffic and exfiltration attempts.

name: Endpoint Denial of Service Detection
description: Detects DoS attacks targeting specific endpoints or services by monitoring resource exhaustion patterns and high-volume requests to single assets
false_positive_notes:
Resource-intensive legitimate operations (batch processing, backups, system updates)
may trigger this rule. Monitor for repeated patterns and correlate with scheduled
maintenance windows to reduce false positives.

name: Drive-by Compromise Detection
description: Detects drive-by compromise attempts by identifying malicious redirects, exploit kit landing pages, and suspicious browser-initiated downloads targeting smart city operator workstations
false_positive_notes:
Ad networks and legitimate redirects may cause false positives. Maintain
a reputation database for known advertising domains and coordinate with
web proxy teams for URL categorization accuracy.

name: External Remote Services Brute Force Detection
description: Detects brute force attacks against externally exposed remote services including RDP, VPN gateways, and SSH endpoints providing access to smart city management networks
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate users with forgotten passwords and automated monitoring systems
checking service availability may trigger this rule. Implement account
lockout policies and correlate with help desk ticket submissions.

name: File and Directory Discovery
description:
Detects enumeration of files and directories on smart city systems:
- Directory listing commands (dir, ls, find, tree)
- Recursive file searches for sensitive file types
- Searching for configuration files, credentials, or keys
- Excessive file system traversal from a single source
- Targeted searches for backup files, database dumps, or scripts
false_positive_notes:
File browsing and search operations are common in normal system use.

Common false positives:
- Backup software scanning directories for changed files
- Antivirus performing file system scans
- Developers searching codebases or log directories

Reduce false positives by:
- Focusing on recursive searches for credential or configuration files
- Monitoring for discovery commands on critical infrastructure hosts
- Correlating with prior unauthorized access or privilege escalation events

name: Firmware Corruption Detection
description: Detects firmware tampering and corruption attempts targeting IoT devices, SCADA controllers, PLCs, and embedded systems within the smart city infrastructure
false_positive_notes:
Authorized firmware updates, OTA update processes, and scheduled device
maintenance may trigger this rule. Coordinate with IoT device management
teams and maintain a firmware version registry for validation.

name: Gather Victim Host Information
description:
Detects attempts to gather information about smart city host systems:
- OS fingerprinting through network probes
- Banner grabbing from exposed services
- SNMP enumeration of host configurations
- Excessive DNS queries for host resolution
- Targeted probing of known management interfaces
false_positive_notes:
Asset management and monitoring systems routinely gather host information.

Common false positives:
- SNMP-based monitoring tools (Nagios, Zabbix)
- Inventory management software querying host details
- Authorized penetration testing activities

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known monitoring and management IPs
- Correlating with unauthorized source IPs
- Flagging queries from external networks targeting internal hosts

name: Gather Victim Identity Information
description:
Detects attempts to harvest identity information from smart city systems:
- LDAP enumeration of user accounts and groups
- Repeated authentication probes with different usernames
- Directory service queries for employee data
- Email address harvesting through SMTP VRFY/EXPN
- Social media scraping targeting city personnel
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate directory services and HR systems query identity information.

Common false positives:
- Active Directory synchronization tools
- HR and provisioning systems querying user directories
- Email distribution list management

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known directory service consumers
- Monitoring for queries from external or unauthorized sources
- Flagging bulk enumeration outside of normal business workflows

name: Gather Victim Network Information
description:
Detects reconnaissance activity aimed at mapping smart city network topology:
- Traceroute and path enumeration
- DNS zone transfer attempts
- Network topology probing via SNMP
- BGP and routing table enumeration
- Excessive ARP requests to discover live hosts
false_positive_notes:
Network management tools routinely perform topology discovery.

Common false positives:
- Network monitoring systems using SNMP for topology maps
- DNS servers performing legitimate zone transfers
- Traceroute utilities used by network engineers

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting authorized network management subnets
- Restricting DNS zone transfers to known secondary DNS servers
- Alerting on topology discovery from non-management VLANs

name: Impair Defenses Detection
description:
Detects attempts to disable or impair security defenses on smart city systems:
- Disabling antivirus, EDR, or firewall services
- Stopping security-related Windows services
- Modifying security tool configurations
- Unloading Sysmon or audit drivers
- Disabling logging or auditing policies
- Tampering with security agent processes
false_positive_notes:
Security tool management may involve stopping and restarting services.

Common false positives:
- Security software updates requiring service restart
- IT administrators reconfiguring firewall rules
- Patch management temporarily disabling services

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known security management consoles
- Monitoring for defense impairment outside of maintenance windows
- Flagging multiple security services stopped in rapid succession
- Correlating with other suspicious activity on the same host

name: Indicator Removal Detection
description:
Detects attempts to remove indicators of compromise from smart city systems:
- Event log clearing or selective deletion
- File deletion of malware artifacts or tools
- Timestamp modification (timestomping)
- History file clearing (bash_history, PowerShell history)
- Network artifact cleanup
- USN journal deletion
false_positive_notes:
Log management and cleanup are part of normal operations.

Common false positives:
- Scheduled log rotation and archival processes
- Disk space management clearing old log files
- Developers clearing shell history for convenience

Reduce false positives by:
- Flagging Security event log clearing (almost always suspicious)
- Monitoring for timestomping (file modification time set before creation time)
- Detecting rapid deletion of multiple log sources
- Correlating with prior suspicious activity on the same host
- Alerting on indicator removal immediately following exploitation events

name: Ingress Tool Transfer Detection
description: Detects transfer of attacker tools and utilities into the environment including wget/curl downloads of suspicious binaries, PowerShell download cradles, and unauthorized file transfers to city infrastructure hosts
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate software downloads, package manager updates, and automated
deployment tools may trigger this rule. Whitelist approved download sources
and software distribution endpoints used by the organization.

name: Input Capture and Keylogging Detection
description: Detects keylogging and input capture activities including keyboard hooking, API-based keystroke logging, and credential interception on smart city operator workstations
false_positive_notes:
Accessibility software, remote desktop tools, and input automation scripts
may exhibit similar behavior. Maintain an approved software inventory and
validate processes against known legitimate input handling applications.

name: IoT Sensor Anomaly Detection
description: Detects anomalous IoT sensor behavior such as excessive event bursts or out-of-range values

name: Kerberoasting Detection
description: Detects Kerberoasting attacks where adversaries request service tickets for service accounts to crack offline, targeting Active Directory integrated smart city management systems
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate service ticket requests during normal authentication workflows
may trigger this rule. Focus on anomalous volumes of TGS requests from
single accounts and correlate with known service account usage patterns.

name: Lateral Movement Detection
description: Detects lateral movement attempts by identifying unusual service-to-service communication, lateral tool transfers, and unauthorized network traversal
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate system administration activities (software deployment, patch management,
configuration updates) may trigger this rule. Establish baselines for normal
administrative traffic patterns and whitelist known management systems.

name: Adversary-in-the-Middle Detection
description: Detects man-in-the-middle attacks including ARP spoofing, DNS poisoning, and LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning targeting smart city network communications and SCADA protocols
false_positive_notes:
Network reconfigurations, DHCP renewals, and legitimate ARP updates may
trigger false positives. Implement static ARP entries for critical
infrastructure and use 802.1X port-based authentication where possible.

name: Create or Modify System Process
description:
Detects creation or modification of system-level processes for persistence:
- Windows service creation with auto-start configuration
- Systemd unit file creation or modification
- Launch daemon installation on macOS
- Modification of existing system service binaries
- Service recovery options changed to execute malicious payloads
false_positive_notes:
System process creation is common during software deployment.

Common false positives:
- Application installers creating new services
- Package managers installing daemon processes
- Configuration management tools deploying service definitions

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known software deployment pipelines
- Monitoring for service modifications outside of change windows
- Flagging services with binaries in non-standard locations
- Detecting service recovery actions pointing to script interpreters

name: Multi-Factor Authentication Bypass Detection
description: Detects MFA bypass attempts including MFA fatigue attacks, push notification bombing, SIM swapping indicators, and token replay attacks targeting smart city administrative accounts
false_positive_notes:
Users with connectivity issues, new device enrollments, and MFA provider
outages may generate multiple authentication attempts. Correlate with
MFA provider status and implement number-matching instead of push approval.

name: Network Port Scan Detection
description: Detects network port scanning activity by monitoring for connections to multiple distinct destination ports from a single source IP within a time window

name: Network Share Discovery
description:
Detects enumeration of network shares on smart city infrastructure:
- net share and net view commands
- SMB share enumeration
- NFS export listing
- Mounting of discovered shares from unauthorized sources
- Rapid traversal of multiple network shares
false_positive_notes:
Network share access is routine for file sharing and collaboration.

Common false positives:
- File servers responding to legitimate share discovery
- IT administrators auditing share permissions
- Backup software enumerating shares for scheduled backups

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known file server management accounts
- Monitoring for enumeration of admin shares (C$, ADMIN$, IPC$)
- Flagging share discovery from non-management workstations
- Correlating with subsequent lateral movement or data staging

name: Network Sniffing Detection
description: Detects network sniffing and packet capture activities including promiscuous mode activation and unauthorized traffic interception on smart city network segments
false_positive_notes:
Network monitoring tools, legitimate traffic analysis, and IDS/IPS sensors
may trigger this rule. Whitelist authorized network monitoring infrastructure
and security appliance interfaces configured for traffic inspection.

name: Obfuscated Command or Script Execution
description:
Detects execution of obfuscated commands and scripts using various techniques:
- Base64 encoded PowerShell commands
- String concatenation and character substitution
- Compression (Gzip, Deflate)
- XOR or other encoding schemes
- Environment variable abuse
- High entropy command lines
false_positive_notes:
Some legitimate software uses obfuscation for various purposes.

Common false positives:
- Software deployment tools using encoded parameters
- Legitimate automation scripts with Base64-encoded configurations
- Application installers with compressed payloads
- Administrative scripts protecting sensitive data

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting signed scripts from trusted vendors
- Excluding known deployment tools (SCCM, Intune)
- Monitoring entropy score (very high entropy = likely malicious)
- Detecting multiple obfuscation techniques in single command
- Correlating with network connections to unknown IPs
- Flagging obfuscation combined with DownloadString/IEX
- Requiring code signing for encoded PowerShell execution

Entropy scoring guide:
- < 4.0: Plain text (normal)
- 4.0-6.0: Moderate complexity (may be normal)
- 6.0-7.5: High entropy (suspicious)
- > 7.5: Very high entropy (likely obfuscated/encrypted)

name: Pass the Hash Detection
description: Detects pass-the-hash attacks where adversaries use stolen NTLM password hashes to authenticate without knowing the plaintext password, enabling lateral movement across city network infrastructure
false_positive_notes:
NTLM authentication in legacy systems and cross-domain trust relationships
may generate similar patterns. Identify systems still requiring NTLM and
work toward Kerberos migration to reduce both risk and false positives.

name: Phishing Activity Detection
description:
Detects general phishing activity targeting smart city personnel:
- Suspicious email attachments with macro-enabled or executable content
- Connections to known phishing infrastructure
- Credential submission to non-corporate domains
- Suspicious OAuth consent flows
- Multiple users accessing the same malicious URL in a short window
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate email with attachments and external links is common.

Common false positives:
- Marketing emails with tracking links
- Legitimate file-sharing services sending notification emails
- Internal phishing simulation exercises

Reduce false positives by:
- Maintaining URL reputation databases and whitelists
- Excluding known phishing simulation platforms
- Correlating with threat intelligence feeds for known phishing domains
- Monitoring for credential entry on non-corporate login pages

name: Spearphishing Link Detection
description: Detects spearphishing link clicks and suspicious URL access patterns indicating social engineering attacks targeting smart city operators through crafted URLs and credential harvesting pages
false_positive_notes:
URL shorteners, marketing email links, and legitimate SaaS login pages may
trigger this rule. Implement URL reputation scoring and maintain a whitelist
of known safe domains used by the organization.

name: Suspicious PowerShell Execution
description:
Detects suspicious PowerShell execution patterns including encoded commands,
execution policy bypasses, hidden windows, and network download attempts.
Common in initial access, execution, and defense evasion phases.
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate administrative scripts may trigger this rule if they use:
- Execution policy bypass for automation
- Encoded commands for complex parameter passing
- Remote script execution from trusted internal repositories

Whitelist known admin workstations and scheduled task hosts.
Consider adding exceptions for scripts signed with trusted certificates.

name: Privilege Escalation Exploit Detection
description: Detects exploitation attempts for privilege escalation including kernel exploits, SUID/SGID abuse, and vulnerability exploitation targeting elevated access on smart city control systems
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate system administration tasks involving sudo, privilege elevation
tools, and automated configuration management may trigger this rule.
Whitelist known administrative accounts and scheduled maintenance processes.

name: Process Injection Detected
description:
Detects process injection techniques including:
- DLL injection using Windows API calls
- Reflective PE injection
- Process hollowing
- Cross-process memory manipulation
- Suspicious rundll32 usage
- PowerShell with memory manipulation
false_positive_notes:
Some legitimate software uses process injection for valid purposes.

Common false positives:
- Antivirus/EDR software injecting into processes for monitoring
- Debugging tools (Visual Studio, WinDbg) during development
- Application compatibility shims
- Legitimate DLL hooking by accessibility tools

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting signed security software
- Excluding developer workstations during debug sessions
- Monitoring for injections into critical processes (lsass, svchost)
- Flagging injections from temporary directories
- Detecting unusual parent-child process relationships
- Correlating with other suspicious activities (credential access, lateral movement)

name: Process Injection Detection (General)
description:
Detects general process injection techniques used for privilege escalation
and defense evasion on smart city systems:
- DLL injection and reflective loading
- Process hollowing and process doppelganging
- Thread execution hijacking
- APC injection and atom bombing
- VDSO hijacking on Linux
- Cross-process memory writes from untrusted sources
false_positive_notes:
Some legitimate software uses process injection for valid purposes.

Common false positives:
- Antivirus and EDR agents injecting into processes for monitoring
- Debugging tools during development sessions
- Application compatibility shims and accessibility tools

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting signed security software
- Monitoring injections into critical processes (lsass, svchost, csrss)
- Flagging injections originating from temp directories
- Correlating with other indicators of compromise

name: Ransomware Activity Detection
description: Detects ransomware encryption activity by identifying mass file encryption events, encryption-related processes, and ransom note indicators
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate encryption operations (data archival, secure file transfers, backup encryption)
may trigger this rule. Establish baseline for normal encryption activity and whitelist
known legitimate encryption processes to minimize false positives.

name: Suspicious Registry Run Key Persistence
description:
Detects additions or modifications to Windows registry run keys commonly
used for persistence. Monitors Run, RunOnce, and other autostart locations
for suspicious entries pointing to temporary directories, PowerShell execution,
or masquerading executables.
technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate software frequently uses run keys for autostart functionality.

Common false positives:
- Software installations adding legitimate autostart entries
- User applications (Dropbox, OneDrive, Slack) adding run keys
- Corporate software (VPN clients, endpoint agents) using run keys

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known application paths (C:\Program Files\*)
- Excluding signed executables from trusted vendors
- Flagging entries with:
  * Executables in \Temp, \AppData\Local\Temp, or Public directories
  * PowerShell or script interpreter execution
  * Command-line parameters with encoding or obfuscation
  * Names similar to system processes (svchost, lsass, explorer variants)
- Monitoring for rapid creation/deletion patterns

name: Remote Services Lateral Movement
description:
Detects abuse of remote services for lateral movement across smart city networks:
- RDP connections from unusual sources
- SSH sessions to critical infrastructure from non-management hosts
- WinRM and PSRemoting from unexpected origins
- VNC connections to IoT management interfaces
- SMB/Windows Admin Shares access from non-admin workstations
- Remote service access outside business hours
false_positive_notes:
Remote administration is essential for managing distributed smart city systems.

Common false positives:
- IT administrators using RDP or SSH for routine management
- Automated deployment tools connecting via SSH or WinRM
- Remote support sessions for IoT device troubleshooting

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known management jump boxes and bastion hosts
- Monitoring for remote service access from non-management network segments
- Flagging connections to multiple hosts in rapid succession
- Correlating with failed authentication attempts preceding successful access

name: Remote Services Exploitation Detection
description: Detects exploitation of remote services including RDP, SSH, SMB, and other exposed services used for lateral movement within the smart city network infrastructure
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate remote administration, automated deployment tools, and IT
management platforms may trigger this rule. Whitelist authorized management
IPs and coordinate with operations teams for scheduled maintenance windows.

name: Resource Hijacking and Cryptojacking Detection
description: Detects resource hijacking including cryptocurrency mining, unauthorized compute usage, and CPU/GPU resource abuse on smart city servers and IoT devices
false_positive_notes:
High CPU usage from legitimate workloads, batch processing, and data
analytics jobs may trigger this rule. Establish baseline resource usage
profiles and correlate with known mining pool domain/IP blocklists.

name: Rootkit Detection
description: Detects rootkit installation and kernel-level persistence including suspicious kernel module loading, hidden process indicators, and system call table modifications on smart city servers and embedded devices
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate kernel module loading during driver installation, system updates,
and hardware provisioning may trigger this rule. Maintain an approved kernel
module whitelist and monitor for unsigned or unexpected module insertions.

name: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation
description:
Detects creation of scheduled tasks with suspicious characteristics:
- SYSTEM privileges
- PowerShell or script execution
- Masquerading as legitimate Windows update tasks
- Tasks running from temporary directories
- Tasks with encoded commands or network activity
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate software installations and updates may create scheduled tasks.

Common false positives:
- Windows Update creating update tasks
- Software installers (Adobe, Google Chrome) creating update tasks
- Antivirus software creating scan tasks
- Backup software creating scheduled backup tasks

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting signed executables from trusted vendors
- Excluding tasks created during known maintenance windows
- Monitoring for tasks with suspicious names mimicking system tasks
- Correlating with recent software installation events
- Flagging tasks that execute from \Temp, \AppData, or user directories

name: Scheduled Task/Job Creation or Modification
description:
Detects creation or modification of scheduled tasks and jobs for persistence
or execution on smart city systems:
- Windows Task Scheduler (schtasks) and Linux cron job manipulation
- AT command scheduling
- Systemd timer creation
- Tasks executing from suspicious paths or with elevated privileges
- Modification of existing legitimate scheduled tasks
false_positive_notes:
Scheduled tasks are commonly used for legitimate system maintenance.

Common false positives:
- Software updates creating scheduled update checks
- Backup software scheduling periodic backup jobs
- System administrators creating maintenance tasks

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting signed executables from trusted vendors
- Monitoring for tasks created outside change management windows
- Flagging tasks that execute scripts from temp or user directories
- Correlating with recent unauthorized access events

name: Screen Capture Activity Detected
description:
Detects attempts to capture screenshots using various methods:
- PowerShell with System.Drawing and System.Windows.Forms
- Graphics.CopyFromScreen API usage
- Automated screenshot loops
- Screenshot capture with network upload
- Third-party screenshot tools (nircmd, etc.)
false_positive_notes:
Screen capture has many legitimate uses.

Common false positives:
- Remote desktop and support tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk)
- Screen recording software (OBS, Camtasia)
- Screenshot utilities (Snagit, Greenshot)
- Monitoring and collaboration tools (Zoom, Teams recording)
- Automated testing frameworks
- Documentation tools

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known screenshot and remote access tools
- Threshold: Requiring 3+ captures in 5 minutes
- Monitoring for captures combined with network upload
- Flagging hidden window execution (WindowStyle Hidden)
- Detecting screenshots saved to temporary directories
- Correlating with other collection activities (keylogging, file staging)
- Excluding captures during known screen sharing sessions

Severity considerations:
- Single screenshot: Low severity (may be legitimate)
- Automated loop (3+ captures): Medium severity
- Capture + network upload: High severity
- Capture + encryption + upload: Critical severity

name: Suspicious Windows Service Creation or Modification
description:
Detects creation or modification of Windows services with suspicious characteristics:
- Service binaries in temporary or user directories
- Services masquerading as legitimate Windows services
- Services executing PowerShell or scripts
- Services with SYSTEM privileges created by non-admin tools
- Modifications to critical Windows services
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate software may create services during installation or updates.

Common false positives:
- Software installers creating legitimate services
- System administrators creating services for monitoring or automation
- Update processes modifying service configurations

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known software installation processes
- Excluding services created by signed installers
- Monitoring for services with binaries in non-standard locations:
  * C:\Windows\Temp
  * C:\Users\*\AppData
  * C:\ProgramData (unless from trusted vendor)
- Flagging services that mimic system service names with slight variations
- Correlating with privilege escalation or lateral movement activities

name: Windows Service Persistence Mechanism
description:
Detects creation or modification of Windows services for persistence:
- Services with binaries in suspicious locations (ProgramData, Public, Temp)
- Services masquerading as legitimate Windows services
- Services running PowerShell or scripts
- Modifications to critical Windows services
- Services with auto-start configured
technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
false_positive_notes:
Some legitimate software creates services in non-standard locations.

Common false positives:
- Third-party software using ProgramData for service binaries
- Update services for browsers and applications
- Monitoring or security software creating services

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting services from signed executables
- Excluding known software vendor service names
- Monitoring for services with:
  * Names similar to Windows services (slight misspellings)
  * Binaries in user-writable directories
  * PowerShell or cmd.exe as service binary
  * SYSTEM privileges combined with suspicious paths
- Correlating with recent compromise indicators
- Flagging services created outside maintenance windows

name: Spearphishing Attachment Detection
description: Detects spearphishing attempts with malicious attachments by monitoring for suspicious email payloads, known malicious file types, and macro-enabled documents targeting city infrastructure personnel
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate bulk email with attachments from known vendors or internal
newsletters may trigger alerts. Maintain a whitelist of known safe senders
and attachment hashes to reduce false positives.

name: SSH Hijacking Detection
description: Detects SSH session hijacking attempts including SSH agent forwarding abuse, session multiplexing exploitation, and unauthorized session takeover on smart city management servers
false_positive_notes:
Legitimate SSH agent forwarding for infrastructure management and automated
deployment pipelines may trigger this rule. Whitelist authorized jump hosts
and review SSH configuration policies for agent forwarding restrictions.

name: Supply Chain Compromise Detection
description: Detects supply chain compromise indicators including unauthorized package installations, tampered software updates, and unexpected dependency changes in smart city infrastructure components
false_positive_notes:
Scheduled software updates and authorized package deployments may trigger
this rule. Coordinate with change management to whitelist planned maintenance
windows and approved software repositories.

name: System Information Discovery
description:
Detects execution of commands and tools used to enumerate system information
on smart city infrastructure hosts:
- systeminfo, uname, hostname, and OS identification commands
- Hardware and software inventory enumeration
- Environment variable harvesting
- Installed software and patch level enumeration
- Rapid succession of discovery commands from a single host
false_positive_notes:
System administrators and automation scripts routinely query system information.

Common false positives:
- Configuration management tools (Ansible, Puppet, Chef)
- Monitoring agents collecting host metrics
- IT inventory and asset management systems

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known management and monitoring accounts
- Excluding scheduled inventory collection scripts
- Monitoring for discovery commands from interactive sessions on critical systems
- Correlating with other reconnaissance or lateral movement activity

name: System Services Abuse Detection
description:
Detects abuse of system services for execution on smart city infrastructure:
- Creation of new services with suspicious binaries
- Modification of existing service configurations
- Service execution from non-standard paths
- Services configured to run with SYSTEM or root privileges
- Launchd, systemd, or Windows service manipulation
false_positive_notes:
Service management is routine for system administration.

Common false positives:
- Software installers creating services during installation
- System administrators deploying new monitoring agents
- Update processes modifying service configurations

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known installer and management tools
- Monitoring for services created from temp or user directories
- Flagging unsigned service binaries
- Correlating with recent privilege escalation or lateral movement

name: System Shutdown and Reboot Detection
description: Detects unauthorized system shutdown and forced reboot commands targeting smart city critical infrastructure including traffic controllers, power grid systems, and water treatment SCADA hosts
false_positive_notes:
Scheduled maintenance reboots, patching cycles, and power management
policies may trigger this rule. Coordinate with operations teams and
correlate with approved change management windows.

name: Access Token Manipulation Detected
description:
Detects attempts to manipulate Windows access tokens for privilege escalation:
- Token impersonation from high-privilege processes
- Token duplication and theft
- SeDebugPrivilege abuse
- Creation of processes with stolen tokens
- Suspicious runas or psexec usage
false_positive_notes:
Token manipulation is used by legitimate software for specific purposes.

Common false positives:
- Task Scheduler running tasks as different users
- Windows services impersonating users
- Administrative tools using RunAs
- Security software accessing process tokens
- Backup software running with SYSTEM privileges

Reduce false positives by:
- Whitelisting known administrative tools (Task Scheduler, services.exe)
- Excluding system processes performing legitimate token operations
- Monitoring for token theft from critical processes (lsass, winlogon)
- Flagging unexpected privilege escalations (user → SYSTEM)
- Detecting access to lsass.exe from non-security software
- Correlating with unauthorized process creation as SYSTEM

name: Traffic Signaling and Port Knocking Detection
description: Detects traffic signaling techniques including port knocking sequences, magic packet triggers, and covert channel activation used to open backdoor access to smart city network services
false_positive_notes:
Wake-on-LAN packets and legitimate port knocking configurations for
authorized remote access may trigger this rule. Document all authorized
port knocking sequences and WoL-enabled devices in the asset inventory.

name: Trusted Relationship Abuse Detection
description: Detects compromise through trusted third-party relationships including vendor access abuse, managed service provider exploitation, and unauthorized third-party connections to city infrastructure
false_positive_notes:
Scheduled vendor maintenance, authorized MSP access, and trusted partner
API integrations may trigger alerts. Maintain a registry of authorized
third-party access windows and correlate with change management records.

name: Valid Accounts Abuse Detection
description: Detects abuse of valid credentials through impossible travel logins, suspicious authentication patterns, and use of compromised accounts across smart city management systems
false_positive_notes:
VPN usage, legitimate travel, and shared accounts may generate false positives.
Correlate with HR travel schedules and VPN connection logs. Implement adaptive
risk scoring based on historical user behavior baselines.

name: Web Application Exploitation Detection
description: Detects web application exploitation attempts including SQL injection, XSS, command injection, and path traversal attacks by analyzing HTTP request patterns
false_positive_notes:
Security scanners, penetration testing tools, and web application firewalls may
generate false positives. Whitelist authorized security testing sources and
coordinate with security teams to reduce noise from legitimate security assessments.
